packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (PARTLY NOT BLIND - SEE EXPOSURE)

Exposure statement - IMPORTANT
- The overviews image-011, image-014 and image-018 show a modern typed slip
  laid beside the fragments, with a typed transcription of chant text and a
  red pencil note ("Stams, STA, Abl. 1v zu Frg. 7-11v"?; faint typed
  "1935" and "Loykam?..." show through). I read that slip in the overview
  BEFORE reading the leaves. It reads (my reading of the typescript):
      Ubi Sampson robustissimus ubi Versucia?
      speciosissimus ubi Versucia?
      Transierunt leges mortaliu(m)
      dies spacium Sed tu deus
        fac te pie nobis xriste pros
      mal erit n...um miserere nobis . .
        anima in morte sumus pie
        s adiutorem nisi te domine
          nostris iuste irasce
        Sancte    deus
        Sancte et misericors  sal-
        emores? nostri ne tradas
  This is an earlier transcription of part of these fragments. Therefore my
  readings of the leaf that carries those words (image-008, image-015, and
  the corresponding parts of the overviews) are NOT blind; they are marked
  [CONTAMINATED] below. The other music spans (image-012, -013, -016, -017,
  -019) do not repeat the slip text, but I have still seen it.
- Background context (an assistant memory index) mentions a "Stams pilot";
  the directory is named "stams-b1-readers"; pencil shelfmarks "Stams, STA,
  Frg. 7-1 ... 7-12" are on the leaves. None names a work.
- Beyond the rules I only made contrast-enhanced, channel-split and mirrored
  crops of supplied tiles in my own scratch directory (mirroring was a test
  for offset text; it did not help and the readings below are from the
  unmirrored images).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Packet covers a group of small parchment pieces "Frg. 7-1" to "7-12"
  photographed in sets of four (overviews image-001, -004, -007, -011, -014,
  -018). Two kinds:
  (a) Pieces with faded, partly erased cursive notes in brown ink
      (German, 14th/15th-c. type documentary cursive), e.g. Frg. 7-4v
      (tiles image-002/-003) and Frg. 7-7v? (tiles image-009/-010), and
      short notes on 7-1v (image-005) and a corner of 7-1v (image-006).
      Many stitching/nail holes and rust stains; one piece has a large
      ruled grid. Mostly unreadable even under enhancement.
  (b) Pieces of a music manuscript: four-line staves (thin ruled lines, no
      red F-line visible), square/rhomboid black notation (Gothic/
      Hufnagel-like rhombs and virgae, custodes at line ends, C-/F-clef
      marks at line starts drawn as a "B/K"-shaped sign), text in a small
      Gothic bookhand below each stave, red strokes touching the capitals
      of each "Ubi" and occasional red vertical division strokes through
      the staves. Two columns per page on at least one piece (7-11v:
      image-012 left col, image-013 right col) with a large decorated
      initial (red/black, cut) at the head of the right column. A smaller
      piece is pasted/folded over 7-11 (image-019).
  Tentative interpretation: a series of rhetorical "Ubi ...?" questions
  (ubi-sunt series) set to music, followed by another chant beginning
  "[A]udi tellus audi ma[gni maris limbus]..." (I report only the letters
  seen). Possibly parts of one music leaf reused in a binding.
- Faces with offset/show-through: image-015 shows notes from both sides
  mixed; image-016/-017 show a second, paler copy of the same text as
  image-012/-013 (another face or an offset; I cannot tell which from these
  crops).

Conventions: [?] unread; word? uncertain; (abc) expansion. Line numbers are
TEXT lines counted from the top of each image (stave lines not counted).

A. MUSIC FRAGMENT, Frg. 7-11v (pencil on image-013 "Stams, STA, Frg. 7-11v")
image-012 (left column; text lines under staves)
t.1  [?]rum? [?]ro? [?]parius? / perpiureus? Ubi alexander   (top line damaged/ abraded)
t.2  rex maximus Ubi stonius? / Ubi histonius? ubi dortissim(us)?   [red-touched U]
t.3  Ubi cum helena paris pulcherrimus
t.4  Achilles ubi magnanimus Ubi cesar
t.5  [?] [?]ag[?]us? ubi hector troie fortiss[imus]   (left part damaged)
t.6  [?]imus Ubi Salomon sapientissimus
image-013 (right column; left edge overlaps image-012 right edge)
t.1  [initial, red and black, cut away] [A]udi tellus audi ma[?]   (edge cut)
t.2  [?]mus? [?]. Audi omne [?]   (abraded)
t.3  [?]e? huius mundi deus e[?]
t.4  sunt falsa [?]?(pro?) historia Con[?]
t.5  temporalia non in uno stat[?]
t.6  [?]a? [?] enim Regum? Regna? [?]   (damaged, under burn holes)

B. SECOND COPY / OTHER FACE OF THE SAME TEXT (paler)
image-017 (left column)
t.1  [?]ora? [?]an? [?] porphirius Ubi alexander
t.2  rex maximus [?] [?] Ubi dortiss[imus]?
t.3  Ubi cum helena paris pulcherrimus
t.4  Achilles ubi magnanimus ubi [?]   (middle abraded)
t.5  [?] ubi [?]agnus? ubi [?] troie fortiss[imus]
t.6  [?]mus Ubi [Sa]lomon sapientissimus
image-016 (right column)
t.1  [initial, red] [?] [?]ellus? audi ma[?]
t.2  [?]mbus? Audi omne a[?]
t.3  sole huius mundi deus e[?]
t.4  sunt falsa [?] historia Con[?]
t.5  temporalia non in uno stat
t.6  [?]il? enim [?]egalis? [?]
  Note: image-016/-017 agree line for line with image-012/-013, so they are
  not new text. Where 012 is damaged, 017 suggests "porphirius" in t.1.

C. PASTED-OVER SMALLER PIECE (image-019, upper-left of 7-11)
t.1  [?]n? congeries Dixit? / Erat? enim rerum
t.2  [?]materies et [?]sit? rerum materies   ("et tu?sit"; abbreviation over u)
t.3  liquescet? a sole glacies Ubi forte[s]? / fortes
t.4  [?] [?] ubi Ioruentius? / Fortunatus? ubi [?]   (torn, folded edge)
t.5  [?] Darius Ubi plato ubi [?]sarius?   (on the darker strip below)
t.6  [?]enim Regum? Regna? [?]   (= image-013 t.6, the strip beneath)
  Left of the pasted piece, the underlying leaf shows "alexander" (top) and
  scraps "[?]parau?" at line ends.

D. MUSIC FRAGMENT WITH SLIP TEXT [CONTAMINATED - not a blind reading]
image-008 (single column, lower part of a music page, Frg. 7-6r?)
t.1  [?]a uita? / [anim]a in morte sumus pie? / pre?   [CONTAMINATED]
t.2  [?] adiutorem n(isi), te domine   [CONTAMINATED]
t.3  [?]ulmerentur? nostris iuste irasce   (first word unclear) [CONTAMINATED]
t.4  [S]ancte  [?]  [d]eus   (spaced, with melisma above) [CONTAMINATED]
t.5  [S]ancte  [?]  et miser[icors] (sal-)   [CONTAMINATED]
t.6  [?]amare? morti ne tradas   (bottom, partly cut) [CONTAMINATED]
image-015 (single column, upper part of a page; text faint with show-
through from the other side)
t.1  [?] [?]speciosissimus? [?]   (top edge) [CONTAMINATED]
t.2  [?] [?] [?]ocusma? / Versucia?   [CONTAMINATED]
t.3  [?]transierunt? leges mortalium   [CONTAMINATED]
t.4  [?] [?]is spacium? Sed [?] tu deus?   [CONTAMINATED]
t.5  fac te pie [?]   [CONTAMINATED]
t.6  [?] [?]   (bottom, under burn hole)
  I cannot claim any of these as independent of the typed slip.

E. DOCUMENTARY NOTES (German cursive, faded/erased)
image-005 (top edge of Frg. 7-1v)
l.1  [?] [?] tauf? [?]   (top edge, cut)
l.2  reyb? / leyb vn(d) gut          ... [right side:] [symbol] dz? ellen vn(d) wassen? / westen?
image-006 (lower corner of 7-1v, faint notes, partly reversed offset?)
  Scraps only: "[?] ogde? / [?] [?]auf? / [?]ard? / oxs? [?] / ottilit?
  [?]" - not usable.
image-002 / image-003 (Frg. 7-4v): faded cursive, about 16 lines; after
  enhancement only isolated words: image-003 t.4 "[?] [?]ra[?] in
  [?]haltige? Ich? [?] zumb? [?]"; t.5 "[?]geben? [?]"; t.8 "[?] wartte?
  [?] [?] [?]loz?"; t.9 "[?] [?] Johann(es)? [?] [?]". Not reliable.
image-009 / image-010 (Frg. 7-7v?): faded cursive in two blocks; the
  clearest lines (image-010 lower right):
  l.1  [?] [?] wollen? Brief? [?] [?]
  l.2  [?] [?]ochstal? / Gotshaus? [?] Stams?
  l.3  [?] [?] [?] [?] Bruder? [?]
  l.4  Item? [?]chof? Burg? [?] [?] [?] [?] [?]
  Not reliable.

AREAS LEFT UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Section D is contaminated by the typed transcription on the slip; treat
  it as non-blind.
- The documentary notes (section E) are largely unread: erased/faded ink
  that did not respond to contrast or channel enhancement. UV imaging would
  be needed.
- Music notation itself was not transcribed (pitches not read).
- Column order on 7-11v assumed left (image-012) then right (image-013)
  from the page geometry; the relation of 7-11v to the pasted piece
  (image-019) and to the paler copy (image-016/-017) is uncertain.
- Top lines of most music pieces are abraded or cut.
